title: HDS Scope
description: A regulation/standard mapped by the HDS matrix, layered on top of the corresponding Pryv platform scope.

layered_on_pryv.description: id of the Pryv scope (vendor/pryv/scopes/<id>.yml) this HDS scope layers on. Optional.

regions.description: Data-residency regions in which this scope is offered (ch = Exoscale/Switzerland, us = AWS/USA).

family.description: Optional grouping key. Scopes sharing a family are presented as one regulation on the site (e.g. the three HIPAA rules), while remaining separate files layered on their own vendor/pryv scope. The family's display name comes from families.yml.

hds_posture.description: HOW HDS ITSELF STANDS against this scope. This is a DIFFERENT axis from hds.coverage on a requirement: coverage says what HDS carries FOR AN IMPLEMENTER, posture says whether HDS as an organisation meets the regulation. Never infer one from the other.

roles.description: The arrangement(s) HDS operates under for this scope. HDS's standing differs by role, so a standing claim that does not name its role is not a claim.

arrangement.description: The arrangement this role covers. THIS MATRIX SCOPES TO THE VAULT PRODUCT: individuals hold their own accounts, data enters only with their explicit consent, and they control who may access it. 'vault' is that product. 'covered-entity-relationship' is the HIPAA case where a Covered Entity is party to the relationship, which is a different statutory test and does not import a GDPR processor role. Any future engagement where HDS genuinely processes on a controller's instructions is out of this matrix's scope and carries its own documentation.

role.description: HDS's role in this arrangement. 'processor' is deliberately NOT available: for the vault product HDS cannot satisfy Art.28(3), because it processes on the individual's permissions rather than a controller's instructions, and cannot delete or return an individual's data at a third party's direction.

applies_to.description: One line: which processing this role covers.

external_assurance.description: Independent assurance HDS holds FOR ITSELF. A hosting provider's certificate is NOT HDS assurance; record those under inherited_provider_assurance.

inherited_provider_assurance.description: Certificates held by hosting providers that HDS relies on but does not hold. Rendered as explicitly NOT HDS's own.

statement.description: 2-4 sentences, plain language, written to be read by someone deciding whether to trust HDS. State the gaps.

known_gaps.description: Named open gaps in HDS's own posture. Each must be anchored: an internal document CODE, a public URL, or the refs of requirements whose planned[] chips carry it.

evidence_backing.description: How much of this scope rests on APPROVED internal documentation. Counts only, never per-document status. This is the honest measure of HDS's position; the row-level `draft` flag measures editorial review of the matrix wording and must never be presented as coverage. Regenerate with scripts/evidence-status.js against a compliance-internal checkout.

rows_evidenced.description: Rows citing at least one internal document.

rows_approved.description: Rows where EVERY cited internal document is approved.

not_a_processor.description: Optional. States why HDS does not hold a processor role for this scope, where a reader would otherwise expect one. Present on the scopes whose regime has a processor concept.
